As Earth swings round the Sun, a nearby star seems to wobble against the distant stars. The size of that wobble gives the star's distance.

Sky view

Where the star appears among the distant stars
Time since first look
Baseline B
Shift of the star, Δ
Parallax p = Δ ÷ B
Distance d = 1 ÷ p

How far can parallax reach?

Distance in parsecs, log scale

A parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit (the Earth–Sun distance) spans one arcsecond: 1 pc is about 206,265 AU, or 3.26 light-years. Parallax is the first rung of the cosmic distance ladder. Brightness-based methods such as Cepheid variables are calibrated against it and take over where parallax runs out.
